findings.summary: Explains the non-detection of magnetic monopoles by quantum uncertainty in phase space. The abstract: Maxwell's dual symmetry predicts monopoles, which have not been detected, and Dirac obtained charge quantization from them; the paper shows that 'the uncertainty in the phase space quantum mechanics could be the responsible of the non-visibility of magnetic monopoles'. Read from the repository's own item page as archived by the Wayback Machine (2021-05-10) and from OpenAIRE's harvest of the repository (2026-08-19). The two-page text (371.pdf) could not be retrieved.
findings.difference: Same question as C3 (why monopoles are not seen) and the same kind of agent, position-momentum (phase-space) quantum uncertainty, which C3's own statement uses (an object compact in momentum is spread in position by about hbar/Delta p). The abstract does not say where the monopoles live: no momentum space, conjugate or p-polarized sector, Born reciprocity, dark matter or abundance, and no claim that position-space searches miss objects compact in momentum. Only the two-page text can show whether its argument is C3's mechanism (which would make it partial) or another use of phase-space uncertainty, and it is still unread. Inference, not read: its 'phase space quantum mechanics' is probably the Kirkwood phase-space picture of Khademi and Nasiri 2008 (J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 128, 012016; C4 related in findings.json), which obtains charge quantization without monopoles. The repository lists Khademi alone; round 3's Zanjan faculty listing gives S. Khademi and S. Nasiri for a talk of the same title at the Multiphysics conference, Lille, December 2009 (not checked). It is the closest item to C3 the check has found.
